references.text: Moses uses the same argument before the Lord—that the Egyptians will hear about it and mock God if He destroys His people after bringing them out of Egypt with great power.
Moses' intercession where he reminds God that He brought the people out of Egypt with His great power, and that other nations will judge God negatively if He destroys His people.
The Lord tells Moses that He will bring Israel out of Egypt with a mighty hand—the same power Moses refers to in his intercession.
Moses reminds the people that the Lord brought them out of Egypt with a mighty hand—the same power he invokes in his intercession.
Continuation of Moses' argument—the nations who have heard about the Lord's power will say that He could not bring the people into the land.
Ezekiel describes how God acted for the sake of His name, so that it would not be dishonored among the nations—the same principle Moses appeals to.
Joshua uses the same argument—what will you do with your great name if the Canaanites hear that Israel has been defeated.
